title: Renal physiology

steps.tx: **Glomerular filtration rate** is determined by Starling forces across glomerular capillaries, where normal net ultrafiltration pressure of approximately 10 to 15 mmHg is driven by glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure opposing plasma oncotic pressure and Bowman space hydrostatic pressure. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: **Tubuloglomerular feedback** operates via macula densa cells sensing sodium chloride delivery through apical NKCC2 cotransporters, releasing adenosine to constrict afferent arterioles and decrease GFR when distal tubular flow rises. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: **Renal autoregulation** maintains renal blood flow and GFR relatively constant across mean arterial pressures ranging from 80 to 180 mmHg via myogenic tone and tubuloglomerular feedback. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: The **proximal convoluted tubule** reabsorbs approximately 65% to 70% of filtered sodium and water, primarily coupled to sodium-hydrogen antiporter 3 (NHE3) and apical sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2). This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: The **thick ascending limb** of Henle generates the medullary hyperosmolar gradient via the apical NKCC2 cotransporter without water reabsorption, establishing the countercurrent multiplier mechanism. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice. Comprehensive nephrology clinical assessment confirms these core diagnostic findings.

steps.tx: The early **distal convoluted tubule** reabsorbs 5% to 7% of filtered sodium via the thiazide-sensitive sodium-chloride cotransporter NCC, while remaining impermeable to water. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice. Comprehensive nephrology clinical assessment confirms these core diagnostic findings.

steps.tx: **cortical collecting duct** is essential. Cortical collecting duct principal cells mediate electrogenic sodium reabsorption via epithelial sodium channels (ENaC) stimulated by aldosterone, creating a lumen-negative potential driving potassium and proton secretion. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: **Free water clearance** is positive in diuresis when urine osmolality is lower than plasma osmolality, and negative during antidiuresis mediated by arginine vasopressin-induced aquaporin-2 translocation to principal cell apical membranes. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.
